items.title: [HQ Admin] Products & Pricing grid picks up wrong column widths on first load
items.desc: Reported live: on page load the frame doesn't pick up the correct dimensions for the HQ Admin product table — it only picks up the correct dimensions once you expand/contract the (platform's) side menu.

notes.author: claude
notes.text:
Root cause: `initGrids()` only sizes the grid's columns once, via a single `requestAnimationFrame` call right at boot, plus a `window` 'resize' listener for later changes. If the Personalisation Hub platform's own iframe hasn't settled to its true final width by that one moment (it can still be finishing its own shell layout — sidebar animating in, other panels still loading), the grid sizes itself against the wrong width and nothing re-checks until an actual 'resize' event happens later. Expanding/collapsing the platform's own sidebar is exactly that — the first thing to genuinely fire 'resize' — which is why it "fixed" it, but only as a side effect.

Fixed by adding a ResizeObserver on `document.body` that runs the same re-fit logic the moment the frame's real size becomes known, instead of relying on one fixed-timing guess at boot. Verified the mechanism in isolation with a Playwright test: after an initial size, changing the container's width via plain CSS (no `resize` event dispatched at all, matching how a platform layout settles) still triggers the re-fit — confirmed by the exact widths recorded across calls, going from 300 to 900 without a resize event in between.

Commit c53cd7c on the feature branch; ready to test.

notes.author: claude
notes.text: Pushed to main as commit `c53cd7c`. Live now.

items.title: [Retail Admin] "Clear local override" does nothing — confirm dialog hidden behind the pricing modal
items.desc: Reported live: 10 Hot Wings at AWS-001 has HQ RRP £6.49 with a corrupted local override at £5.99. Clicking "Clear local override" in the Pricing tab and confirming did nothing — the price stayed at £5.99.

notes.author: claude
notes.text:
Found it: the confirm dialog (#confirmOverlay) has z-index 200, but the item detail modal it opens on top of has z-index 300. So when “Clear local override” is clicked from inside the Pricing tab (the modal is still open), the confirm dialog renders *behind* the modal — invisible. A real mouse click on “Clear override” just hits the modal underneath and does nothing, which matches exactly what you saw. (My first reproduction attempt used a scripted `.click()` call, which bypasses real hit-testing and doesn't see stacking-order bugs like this — that's why it looked fine to me at first; a real Playwright mouse click reproduced the failure immediately once I tried it that way, and confirmed the fix.)

Fixed by raising the confirm dialog to z-index 400, above the modal. Verified with a real (non-scripted) mouse click end-to-end: your exact numbers (RRP £6.49, corrupted local override £5.99) now correctly resolve to £6.49 after clicking Clear override and confirming.

Separately: you mentioned a “Targeted” pill under “Badge for External Displays” for this product — that's the real Personalisation Hub platform's own per-product editor, not this repo's code (confirmed earlier — that phrase doesn't exist anywhere in this codebase), so it's an unrelated platform feature and doesn't affect this pricing bug or its fix.

Commit 11e1a67 on the feature branch; ready to test.

notes.author: claude
notes.text: Confirms it — "appearing underneath the standard product model" is exactly the z-index bug (confirm dialog at 200, pricing modal at 300) I found and fixed above. Same root cause, same fix (commit 11e1a67).

items.title: [Backend] Generate Video's hero videos go dead after some time (8 PC Boneless Banquet, Family Fish Bucket, 10 Hot Wings)
items.desc: Reported live: several products' primary-tile videos on the menu board stopped working — showing a broken-media placeholder instead — while others (10 pc Bucket, 6 pc Bucket) kept working fine. Confirmed this was not caused by the two pricing commits just published (they only touch retail-admin.html's pricing pane).

notes.author: claude
notes.text:
Found the real cause, and it's a backend one: the generateProductVideo Cloud Function (Product Assets → Generate Video) returns the AI video provider's own result URL directly — and that URL is only hosted temporarily by the provider. So a hero video that worked perfectly the day it was generated quietly goes dead some time later with no code or data change anywhere near it, while a directly-uploaded photo/video (stored as a permanent data: URI in Firestore itself) never has this problem. That matches exactly what you're seeing: the broken items are the ones with an AI-generated hero video; 10 pc Bucket/6 pc Bucket are presumably using an uploaded asset instead.

Fixed by having the function download the generated video the moment it's ready and re-host it in this project's own Cloud Storage bucket, returning a signed URL with a far-future expiry instead of the provider's own link — permanent, the same guarantee an upload already has. If re-hosting fails for any reason it falls back to today's behaviour (the provider's own URL) rather than breaking video generation outright. Commit d5a9896 on this branch (not yet on main).

Two important things this does NOT do on its own:
1. It doesn't retroactively fix the videos already broken — 8 PC Boneless Banquet, Family Fish Bucket, 10 Hot Wings (and possibly others using Generate Video) will need their hero video regenerated (or the affected asset re-uploaded) once this fix is live, so the new generation gets a permanent URL this time.
2. This is a Cloud Functions change, not a static-site one — pushing it to `main` does NOT deploy it. Someone with Firebase deploy access needs to run `firebase deploy --only functions` (or `npm run deploy` inside menu-board-demo/functions) — this sandbox has no Firebase CLI or credentials, so I can't run that step myself.

Ready to test (after deploying): use Generate Video on a product, confirm the resulting hero video plays, then check the saved src is a storage.googleapis.com URL rather than the video provider's own domain — that's the signal it's now permanently hosted.

notes.author: claude
notes.text: Pushed to main as commit `d5a9896` (carried onto main by the same push as commit `45d679b`). Live for the *code*, but this touches menu-board-demo/functions/ (a Cloud Function), which GitHub Pages does not serve — main being updated does NOT make this fix active. Whoever has Firebase deploy access still needs to run `firebase deploy --only functions` (or `npm run deploy` inside menu-board-demo/functions) before new videos actually get re-hosted permanently. This also doesn't retroactively fix the three videos already broken (8 PC Boneless Banquet, Family Fish Bucket, 10 Hot Wings) — those need to be regenerated again after the functions deploy goes out.

Verified end-to-end in a stubbed-Firebase browser test: before clearing the grid showed a corrupted £5.99; after, it correctly falls back to HQ's real RRP with no override remaining in storePricing at all. Commit ad986f7 on this branch (not yet on main).

For 10 Hot Wings specifically at store AWS-001: once this ships, open it in Retail Admin, use "Clear local override" to wipe the corrupted record, then (if a local offer is still wanted there) re-enter it fresh — RRP left alone at HQ's £6.49, Offer price set to £5.99, and a Show on Menu Board note if you want the badge.

Ready to test: open a product with a store override, confirm "Clear local override" appears and is absent when there's no override, confirm the confirmation dialog reads correctly, and confirm clearing it removes the override entirely (price/badge revert to HQ's own everywhere — the table, the pricing pane, and the menu board).

items.title: [HQ Admin] Can't reorder Price/Description in Local Feature Highlight tile layout
items.desc: Editing the Local Feature Highlight (Feature Hero Spotlight) board's Tile Layout, unable to move items on the right (Secondary/Promo tile) up and down to reorder price and description — doesn't fit the model any more.

notes.author: claude
notes.text: Found it — this is a side effect of the Price + Offer Badge combining work from earlier today. A Local Feature Highlight template saved before that change still carries Price and the Offer Badge as two separate entries in its Tile Layout. The editor's own element list no longer has a listing for either of those on their own (only the combined "Pricing (Price + Offer Badge)" item), so a legacy template showed up as two raw, unrecognised rows there instead of one clean "Pricing" row — and "Pricing" still looked available to add on top, so adding it left three pricing-shaped rows tangled together in that zone. Trying to move Price or Description around that mess is what broke. Fixed by migrating a legacy Price+Badge pair into one "Pricing" row automatically the moment a template like this is opened for editing, matching what a template built today already looks like. Commit 2c93386 on this branch (not yet on main). Ready to test: open the Local Feature Highlight template's Tile Layout editor, check the Secondary (right-hand) tile's section, and confirm Price now shows as a single row you can freely reorder against Description and everything else.

notes.author: claude
notes.text: Fixed the test link itself — it was pointing at the published site on main, which obviously doesn't have an unpublished fix on it yet. Switched it to raw.githack.com, a free proxy that serves a file straight from a specific GitHub branch with the right content-type so it actually renders as a page instead of raw text — pointed at this fix's branch specifically, so it reflects exactly what's pending, not what's live. I can't reach raw.githack.com myself to confirm it loads (this sandbox's network is locked down to a short allowlist) — if it doesn't work for you, tell me and I'll switch to a plain 'here's the branch and file path, please pull it locally' note instead.

notes.author: claude
notes.text: Found the real cause of the cut-off controls, thanks to your screenshot — it let me measure the exact overflow. This editor lives in the same shared brand-edit dialog every tab uses, which is fixed at 680px wide regardless of your screen or the iframe around it. The two-column layout had a responsive breakpoint meant to stack into one column on a narrow screen — but it was checking the outer window's width, not the 680px dialog's own width, and the outer window is almost always well above that breakpoint even though the dialog itself never was. So it stayed two columns, each squeezed into barely 300px, and the align/reorder/delete controls got pushed off the edge. Reproduced it precisely (a 636px-wide container overflowed by 103px, matching your screenshot almost exactly) and fixed it by just always stacking Primary above Secondary — there's no real screen size where two columns would ever fit in this dialog anyway, so the conditional layout was never buying anything. Commit fc67ed3 on this branch (not yet on main; same test link as before, now updated). Ready to test: open the Local Feature Highlight template's Tile Layout editor and confirm every row's align/up/down/delete controls are now fully visible and clickable, with Secondary Tile stacked below Primary instead of beside it.

Read through the full wiring: the Gap number field → _renderPricingPreview() → an inline flex `gap` style on the preview span, and the same value → savePricingDisplay() → Firestore → pricingBlockHtml() on the real board, which applies it the same way. No margin or CSS rule anywhere overrides that inline gap. I then actually drove it live in a real browser (this sandbox can't reach Firebase/AG Grid's CDN, so I stubbed those two out to let the rest of the page run for real) and measured the rendered preview: setting the field to 38 produced an exact 38px gap between the badge and price, pixel for pixel. notes.author: claude
notes.text: Reopening this — your report that it's still not right on the Featured menu board and the Personalised Featured menu board ("the Local [Feature Highlight]") pointed at something my first fix only partly addressed. The real problem: on those boards, when a template's layout still has Price and the Offer Badge as two separate elements (from before an earlier update combined them), they're two independent children of the hero panel's own layout box — which has its own small fixed spacing between its children. My first fix just added extra margin to the badge, which stacked on top of that fixed spacing rather than replacing it, so the setting still wasn't the true distance. Proper fix now: that adjacent pair renders through the exact same combined element a new template's "Pricing (Price + Offer Badge)" uses, so the whole account-wide setting — gap and placement both — genuinely governs it, on the Featured and Personalised Featured boards specifically, same as everywhere else. notes.author: claude

items.title: [Shared] Performance pass: table loads, personalised offers, product tables
items.desc: Performance pass across HQ Admin table load, Retail Admin table load, personalised offer loading, and product table loading. Remove unused code and optimise page loading; personalised offers should update immediately when the underlying data changes via the PH API. Touches both HQ Admin and Retail Admin. (Source: backlog sheet #5)

notes.author: claude
notes.text:
Found and fixed one concrete issue: renderItems() in Retail Admin computed its visible-items list (which includes a per-item brand lookup) and then immediately called updateSummaryBar(), which recomputed that exact same list with its own separate brand scan — so every items/stock/localFeatured/pricing change scanned every item against the brand list twice. updateSummaryBar() now reuses the list renderItems() already built instead of redoing that work. Commit f7d26fc on claude/ph-prototype-odqyzs.

Also checked and ruled out, so I don't re-tread this ground: the earlier brand-lookup Map cache (already live) is being used correctly everywhere else I could find; Firestore listeners are each registered exactly once in HQ Admin, Retail Admin, and the menu board — no duplicate subscriptions; the menu board's own snapshot handlers already skip re-rendering when nothing actually changed; and both admin grids already use AG Grid's own recommended getRowId-based diffing rather than a full rebuild on every snapshot, so that's not a bug either. One small, low-priority item I did NOT fix: HQ/Retail Admin's Menu Types column cellRenderer does the same shape of per-tag .find() the brand lookup used to, but against a list of HQ-configured menu types that's realistically a handful of entries, not hundreds — not worth the churn on its own. I didn't find anything to support "remove unused code" specifically — nothing genuinely dead turned up in the time I spent looking, and I'd rather say that than invent something to remove.

Ready to test: this is a background performance fix with no visible behaviour change — Retail Admin's summary bar (Active/In Stock/Out of Stock counts) should look and update exactly as before, just doing less duplicate work underneath.

items.title: [Retail Admin] One-click revert to RRP + stuck bucket offer
items.desc: At store level, add a one-click “Return to RRP” CTA for when a store is running a special promotion — pressing it plus Save Changes should revert pricing to RRP once stock is sold out. Also: the current store has a 10-piece bucket offer stuck and unable to be cleared — fix that specific stuck state, and test that stores can still set a special offer and quickly revert to RRP afterwards. (Source: backlog sheet #10)

notes.author: claude
notes.text: The actual bug: a blank offer price does NOT mean "no offer" in this data model — this store's own override only takes effect once it carries its OWN priced offerPrice; a blank one falls straight through to whatever HQ has configured, recurring offers included. That's why the bucket offer was stuck — clearing the field looked like it worked but the HQ recurring offer just kept coming back on its own schedule. Added a "Return to RRP" button that instead sets this store's offer price equal to RRP itself (a valid, priced override that wins outright, forces the recurrence off, and clears the schedule/promo copy) — the existing offerPrice===RRP check already suppresses any strikethrough/discount display everywhere it's read, so this store just shows plain RRP. Commit 665af92 on claude/ph-prototype-odqyzs. Ready to test: on the store carrying the stuck 10-piece bucket offer, open its pricing, hit Return to RRP, Save, and confirm it actually stops discounting (including after the page reloads) — then confirm you can still set a fresh special offer afterwards.

notes.author: claude
notes.text:
Shipped as "Magic Edit" — the old Touch Up icon/tool, renamed and expanded, and no longer gated behind Background removal having run first (it's now always clickable on any non-video image, per the ask). Added: Crop (drag a corner to resize the selection, drag inside to move it, Apply Crop trims the photo) and Zoom in/out for precise brush work on a large photo. The Restore/Erase brush from before is unchanged.

One deliberate scope call: I kept Crop/Restore/Erase non-AI, same reasoning Remove Background and Enhance moved AWAY from Gemini's generative edit for (see that code's own comment on why) — a deterministic tool can't behave unpredictably the way a generative call can. "Closer to Canva's Magic Eraser" specifically usually means AI object removal + inpainting (paint over something, it vanishes and the background fills in around it) — genuinely different from this Erase mode, which paints transparency rather than filling in content. I didn't build that: it would mean a second AI call with exactly the reliability risk this codebase already backed away from once. Happy to build it if you do want that specific AI behavior — just flag it and I'll scope it as its own item rather than guess.

Commit 70e2c2a on claude/ph-prototype-odqyzs. Ready to test: open Magic Edit on a fresh, untreated image (confirm it's no longer greyed out), try Crop (drag corners, drag to move, Apply), try Zoom in/out while painting, and confirm Restore/Erase still work as before.

items.title: [HQ Admin] Video prompt not cleared between generations
items.desc: The previously used video-generation prompt is being reused when starting a new video generation for the same product with a different prompt. Clear the prompt field when starting a new generation. (Source: backlog sheet #7)

notes.author: claude
notes.text: Fixed: openVideoModal() now resets the prompt field to the configured/default prompt every time the modal opens, instead of only once ever. Commit c40a552 on claude/ph-prototype-odqyzs. Ready to test: generate a video with a custom prompt, then open Generate Video again (same or different product) and confirm the field shows the default prompt, not the previous custom one.

notes.author: claude
notes.text:
Checked the full path for this — I don't think there's a code bug left here. confirmGenerateVideo() reads videoPrompt fresh at click time (not a stale closure), threads it straight through generateProductVideo() → the generateProductVideo Cloud Function (functions/index.js) → the video provider's POST body's own `prompt` field on every call, and each call gets a brand-new job id from the provider and polls that job specifically. So a different prompt is genuinely being sent, and a genuinely new video comes back each time — nothing here reuses or caches a previous result.

What's left is outside this repo: a single fixed source photo plus a short, camera_motion:'static' turntable-style clip gives an image-to-video model very little to work with, and for a small prompt tweak (an adjective, a mood word) some providers barely vary the output — the source image dominates far more than the text does. Two things would help me dig further rather than guess: (1) does the AI Providers → Video provider dashboard show two separate job ids for the two generations, and (2) how different was the prompt wording — a small tweak vs. a completely different scene/action? If it's the latter and still barely changes, that points at the provider/model itself rather than anything fixable here.
